tagline: A long loop around a river that turned into a lake.
intro: The trail is a loop of two-lane roads on both banks of the Tennessee River, 440 miles of them, the longest scenic byway in the state. From the eastern gateway on I-40, TN 13 runs north through Waverly to Erin and the road carries on to Dover on the Cumberland. From there it goes west to the river at Paris Landing and on to Paris, comes south through Camden and Parsons to Savannah, and returns north through Waynesboro and Linden.
Part of the river along here is Kentucky Lake now. When the TVA dammed it in 1944, the water covered the town of Johnsonville, which had stood only since 1864.

moments.title: Fort Donelson
moments.text: On the Cumberland just below Dover, Grant took the fort in February 1862, one of the first major Union successes of the war, and Nashville fell to the Union within weeks.

moments.title: Paris Landing State Park
moments.text: The park stands inland from the original Paris Landing, a steamboat stop that went under Kentucky Lake when the river was dammed.

moments.title: Savannah
moments.text: The river town began as Rudd's Ferry, and in 1862 Grant commandeered the Cherry Mansion off its square as headquarters for the battle at Shiloh, ten miles to the southwest.
